Create a heatmap

Source: R/heatmap_chart.R
heatmap_chart.Rd

Draws a grid of coloured cells, one per combination of two categorical columns, coloured by a value (or by the number of rows when value is NULL). Rows sharing the same pair are aggregated. With a midpoint, the colours diverge around it (useful for correlations or changes); with cluster = TRUE, the rows and the columns are reordered by hierarchical clustering so that similar ones sit together.

Usage

heatmap_chart(
  data,
  x,
  y,
  value = NULL,
  aggregate = c("sum", "mean", "median", "min", "max"),
  colors = NULL,
  midpoint = NULL,
  cluster = FALSE,
  show_values = NULL,
  value_format = ",.2~f",
  cell_gap = 1,
  cell_radius = 2,
  na_col = "#f2f2f2",
  legend = TRUE,
  x_title = NULL,
  y_title = NULL,
  axis_title_font_size = 12,
  x_font_size = 11,
  y_font_size = 11,
  hover = TRUE,
  animate = TRUE,
  title = NULL,
  title_font_size = 16,
  font = "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif",
  bg_col = "white",
  text_col = "#333333",
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame.

x, y

The names of the columns giving the columns and the rows of the grid. Factor levels give the order.

value

Optional. The name of a numeric column giving the colour. When NULL, cells count the rows of each pair.

aggregate

How to combine several rows of the same pair: "sum" (the default), "mean", "median", "min" or "max".

colors

The colour ramp, from low to high (two colours or more). By default a light to dark blue ramp, or red - white - blue with a midpoint.

midpoint

Optional. A value at the centre of a diverging colour ramp (e.g. 0 for correlations). The ramp is symmetric around it.

cluster

Logical. Reorder the rows and columns by hierarchical clustering (stats::hclust()). Defaults to FALSE.

show_values

Logical. Write the values in the cells. By default they are shown when the cells are large enough.

value_format

A d3 format for the values. Defaults to ",.2~f".

cell_gap

The gap between cells in pixels. Defaults to 1.

cell_radius

The corner radius of the cells in pixels. Defaults to 2.

na_col

The colour of missing pairs. Defaults to "#f2f2f2".

legend

Logical. Show the colour legend. Defaults to TRUE.

x_title, y_title

Optional. The titles of the axes.

axis_title_font_size

The font size of the axis titles. Defaults to 12.

x_font_size, y_font_size

The font sizes of the labels. Default to 11.

hover

Logical. Show tooltips and highlight on hover. Defaults to TRUE.

animate

Logical. Fade the cells in when the chart is drawn. Defaults to TRUE.

title

Optional. The title of the chart.

title_font_size

The font size of the title. Defaults to 16.

font

The font family. Defaults to "Verdana, Geneva, Tahoma, sans-serif".

bg_col

The background colour. Defaults to "white".

text_col

The colour of the text. Defaults to "#333333".

width, height

Optional. The size of the chart.

Value

An r2d3 htmlwidget.

Interactions

Hover a cell to see its value, outline it, highlight its row and column labels and mark it on the colour legend. Cells fade in diagonally when the chart is drawn. Inside Shiny, clicking a cell sets input$<id>_clicked to a list with x, y and value.

Examples

# A correlation matrix
cors <- as.data.frame(as.table(cor(mtcars)))
names(cors) <- c("var1", "var2", "correlation")
heatmap_chart(cors, x = "var1", y = "var2", value = "correlation",
              midpoint = 0, cluster = TRUE, title = "Correlations in mtcars")



# Average temperature by month and day of the week
aq <- airquality
aq$Month <- factor(month.abb[aq$Month], levels = month.abb[5:9])
aq$Week <- paste("Week", (aq$Day - 1) %/% 7 + 1)
heatmap_chart(aq, x = "Month", y = "Week", value = "Temp", aggregate = "mean",
              colors = c("#fff3d6", "#ffb15c", "#d6402b"),
              value_format = ".0f", title = "Temperature in New York (F)")



# Counts of two categorical variables
heatmap_chart(ggplot2::mpg, x = "class", y = "manufacturer", show_values = TRUE)
